Concerted Prayer: Prayer is the foundation of all Christian endeavor. It is through prayer that God works to advance His Kingdom. It is significant that our Lord's command is to pray that He will send the laborers. We call upon the General Assembly to join in focused, concerted prayer for the advancement of the Kingdom through church planting. Only if the Spirit of God is at work through our efforts will our efforts be effective in advancing the Kingdom.

By God's power, lives are transformed by the Gospel as we wait upon Him in prayer. GA/MNA communication pieces, Multiply and the web site (pcanet.org), give a high priority to prayer by suggesting weekly prayer requests on a regional basis for the advancement of the church. The Intercessor for all regions may be accessed on the web site, offering greater opportunity for intercession for ministry across North America.

Recruiting Church Planters: In 2000, a record number of assessed and qualified church planters were presented to the GA/MNA Committee for approval. The GA/MNA staff is giving high priority to recruiting during 2001 in order to increase men available for assessment and approval for church planting. As churches increase their Partnership Share/Askings giving, more resources will be devoted to recruiting church planters. Assessing Potential Church Planters: GA/MNA's Church Planting Assessment is highly effective and now developed as one of the finest assessments in America. In 2001 GA/MNA will seek to expand the number of assessment events that are produced to accommodate a higher level of recruitment. The primary focus of these assessments is the evaluation for competencies that are particular to church planting. Among these competencies are character qualities such as integrity, spiritual vitality, prayer, humility, and godliness in family leadership; ministry competencies such as evangelism, leadership, preaching, and leadership development; personal competencies such as

532

<a id="ga29-p535"></a>
<!-- PAGE ga=29 pdf_page=535 printed_page=533 -->

flexibility, emotional stability, sensitivity to people, dynamism, likeability, and the church planter and his family's calling to this task.

Placing Church Planters on the Field: The placement process begins with a church planter committing to a set of biblical core values which God has put on his heart. These values form the foundation of a vision that will shape the church. After the vision is solidified and documented, the location that will best facilitate this vision is then determined by a sense of the Lord's call to the church planter, and mutual agreement with the presbytery, in consultation with the GA/MNA church planting staff. GA/MNA staff then offer assistance to the presbytery and the church planter in the many practical steps and administrative details that are necessary to begin the work.

Men are being assessed, qualified, and placed in many different demographic situations. Some in places where there are core groups who wish to have a new church, others where there is no core group but still great need. Also men are being place in many different demographic profiles. Some areas are large cities, others are smaller communities, both with a sensitivity to recognize where there is need and where God is at work.

Training Church Planters: GA/MNA offers five different types of church planter training, each addressing different needs. All PCA church planters, whether or not they participated in the GA/MNA assessment process, and regardless of their funding sources or sources of oversight, are invited to take advantage of these training resources.

1. The National Church Planter Training Conference — In 2000 this conference was held August 7-10, and in 2001 will be held August 13-16 in the Atlanta area for all PCA church planters, their wives, leaders in church planting churches, presbytery GA/MNA chairmen and committee members, and church planting network leadership. This training is "curriculum driven" which means that the various seminars and workshops are designed to respond to the different phases of the life of a church plant (start-up phase, ministry building phase, organization phase, and the reproduction phase).

2. Regional Training Conferences — The curriculum is complementary to the national training. However, by taking advantage of the smaller numbers than attend the national conference, and by addressing issues unique to each region, these events provide a more specific curriculum, a more personal level of interaction, and more individualized coaching.

3. Bootcamp — GA/MNA's church planter boot camps are workshop oriented, practical, two-day training experiences, which are now offered directly following each church planting assessment. These boot camps are designed to provide the working environment and coaching to assist the church planter in the development of working plans such as establishing core values, formulating vision, philosophy of ministry, fundraising, developing learning contracts, and

533

<a id="ga29-p536"></a>
<!-- PAGE ga=29 pdf_page=536 printed_page=534 -->

church planting strategy for the new church start. This training focuses in greater detail on the initial stages of the church plant.

4. Coaching Retreats — These retreats are designed with the individualized needs of the church planter in mind. The group is small, and the ratio of church planters to coaches as small as possible (2 to 1). The coaches are experienced church planters who are skilled in the process of assisting the church planter in working through the unique needs of his particular church planting experience.

5. Church Planting Apprenticeships — The GA/MNA Church Planting Apprenticeship is designed for men whom GA/MNA recognizes are quality church planting candidates but lack the kind of experience that will equip the man to plant a church. The apprenticeship focuses on the development of the church planter in the specific areas of concern found by the assessment and offers church planting candidates the opportunity to develop with a mentor in preparation for starting a new church, often as a project sponsored by the mentoring church. In 2000 GA/MNA invested $154,500 in 12 men through the Timothy Fund to assist such apprenticeships.

Coaching Church Planters in the Process: In addition to the coaching retreats mentioned above, GA/MNA offers the church planter direct consultation by staff, and assistance in establishing mentoring relationships for each church planter. Regional coordinators, movement leaders, Presbytery MNA Chairmen, and church planting network leaders also play a major role in the coaching process, or in identifying others who may assist the church planter.

Building a Denominational Team of Church Planting Leadership: As the vision for church planting continues to grow among particular churches, presbyteries, and among church planting networks (which include a wide variety of formal and informal structures), GA/MNA fulfills a growing role of serving, coordinating and taking the initiative to develop the resources necessary for the vision for an advancing church to be fulfilled. GA/MNA brings this leadership through several avenues:

Regional Coordinators: GA/MNA Regional Coordinators serve churches that want to reproduce themselves with daughter churches, and presbyteries that are proactive in multiplying churches. They assist launch teams (core groups) and presbytery MNA chairmen in recruiting church planters. Regional Coordinators assist in the assessment process as assessors. They assist the church planters in the development of their strategic plan to move to the field, help them develop learning contracts, assist church planters with fundraising, and provide valuable counsel regarding choosing the location for the church. They provide valuable coaching to the church planters through the process of starting the church, and serve the presbytery MNA committees in their geographic areas by helping to identify areas where new churches are needed when there is no launch team. All regional coordinators serve on a limited part-time or volunteer basis.

534

<a id="ga29-p537"></a>
<!-- PAGE ga=29 pdf_page=537 printed_page=535 -->

Presbytery MNA Chairmen: GA/MNA works closely with many presbytery MNA chairmen as they provide church planting leadership in their presbyteries. On November 6-7, 2000, GA/MNA hosted what will become an annual National Conference for Presbytery MNA Chairmen. The 2001 Conference will be held in Atlanta on October 29-31. The goal of this conference is to offer seminars and workshops to presbytery MNA committee chairmen and members, seeking to equip them as a primary force in church multiplication in their presbyteries.

Church Planting Networks: GA/MNA is active in the process of encouraging the development of church planting networks. A church planting network is simply a group of churches that combine time, talent and treasure to plant churches more effectively together than they could do separately. Some are highly structured and defined, while others are more informal. GA/MNA encourages all such efforts that enhance the ability of particular churches and presbyteries to fulfill their calling to build church planting movements.

- **B.** Multicultural Ministries

State of the Task

During 2000, we continued to witness a growing interest and commitment in the PCA to communicate the Gospel among ethnic groups that are rapidly growing in North America. Several states are already at least 51% non-white in composition, or are very close to it. Around the year 2050 the growth of ethnic population groups will be such that over 50% of the total population of the United States will be non-white. Some time before the year of 2004, there will be more Hispanics in the United States than there are African Americans. The PCA, historically motivated and recognized for its Matthew 28 Great Commission zeal and efforts, now has an unprecedented cross-cultural evangelistic opportunity and challenge right at its own front door. These growing groups are our "Samaritan" mission field (Acts 1:8-9).

The growing interest in multicultural ministries and church planting is observed in part in the following ways: Church and presbytery leaders communicate frequently with GA/MNA personnel seeking help in evangelizing ethnic groups as part of the changing demographics surrounding their churches; An increasing number of second-generation leaders from various ethnic backgrounds are entering reformed seminaries and non-traditional presbytery sponsored leadership training programs; Presbyteries are designing and implementing non-traditional ways to train and credential Teaching Elders (in accordance with PCA standards) from within the ethnic groups in which churches need to be planted. Articles in Multiply and Intercessor have highlighted multicultural church planting and have generated much interest and response. There is an increasing interest by some presbyteries, churches, and church planters to start churches that are intentional in reaching the ethnic populations in their geographical areas.

537

<a id="ga29-p540"></a>
<!-- PAGE ga=29 pdf_page=540 printed_page=538 -->

A few PCA churches, instead of selling their property and moving, have made an intentional decision to change in order to continue to reach out to the changing cultural and demographic changes around them.

The purpose of GA/MNA Multicultural Ministries is to encourage and initiate reformed church planting among ethnic people that results in Gospel movements that saturate these people groups.

The term multicultural is used by GA/MNA in two ways. (1) To describe the work of ethnic-specific church planting through which congregations are formed that are largely homogeneous and non-white; (2) To describe specific churches who include leaders and members from a variety of ethnic backgrounds, worshipping and serving God together.

Advances in 2000

Ethnic and multicultural church planters continue to be assessed, placed, and coached in church planting. Some of GA/MNA's assessment centers have seen over 50% of the candidates be multicultural in focus.

There are now around 20 African American teaching elders in the PCA and another five men in seminaries. TE Wy Plummer is MNA African American Movement Leader.

We are actively preparing for the assessment of new ethnic church planters by trained leaders from within their own ethnic communities.

There continues to be major Korean first-generation participation in the PCA with TE Henry Koh providing leadership as MNA Korean Ministries Coordinator. Many second- generation/English speaking Koreans are enrolled in reformed seminaries and are anxious to begin multicultural English speaking congregations around the PCA. The first ever Korean EM (English Ministry) conference was held in January of 2000.

MNA Brazilian Movement Leader TE Osni Ferreira, now counts 13 Brazilian congregations who together have committed $30,000 towards a new PCA Brazilian church plant somewhere in the United States.

The PCA now counts four Haitian churches and church plants in the United States with a fifth plant planned for 2001. Several Haitian leaders are in seminary. A PCA presbytery on the island of Haiti is being discussed and planned by MNA, MTW, and members of Southern Florida Presbytery. Dony St. Germain is MNA Haitian Movement Leader.

The most significant advance in terms of addressing the need for more ethnic church planters is the focus on training ethnic leaders through the use of church planting

538

<a id="ga29-p541"></a>
<!-- PAGE ga=29 pdf_page=541 printed_page=539 -->

apprenticeship programs, through which men who appear to have the gifts and skills for church planting work under the mentoring leadership of a church planting pastor, prior to their taking the lead in planting a church on their own.

Korean Ministries

Reaching "First Generation" Koreans (those who were born in Korea, and for whom Korean is their primary language for worship, as well as for everyday discourse within their communities):

There are over 180 PCA Korean language churches which are members of seven Korean language presbyteries. TE Henry Koh, GA/MNA Korean Ministries Coordinator, serves these churches with a particular focus on encouraging their participation in the fellowship and financial support of the PCA, and in working with the Korean pastors in their commitment to the reformed faith.

The annual conference of the Coalition of Korean Churches in PCA met at Korean First Presbyterian Church, in Tucker, GA, from February 5-7, 2001 with the conference theme of "The Churches that are Advancing Ahead". The purpose of the Coalition is to maintain Christian fellowship and close relationships among Korean churches in the PCA and to discuss and carry out ministry activities in cooperation with one another.

Pastor Dong Ho Kim of Dong-An Presbyterian Church, in Seoul, Korea was the main speaker of the event. MNA Coordinator TE James Bland also gave an encouraging greeting at the dinner meeting on the opening night. New president and officers of the Coalition were chosen during this annual event. The Korean Women in the Church (WIC) also conducted their own seminars, elected a new president and discussed their annual project. WIC has finished the translation and the publication of the book, Leadership for Women in the Church, by Susan Hunt. Nearly 2000 copies have been distributed to Korean churches in the PCA.

All of the brochures in the IAR are now translated into the Korean language. The Korean Ministries Coordinator, TE Henry Koh, is encouraging Korean churches to participate especially in the Tax Sheltered Annuity plan for their pastors. Many churches have responded positively but it is yet far from the goal.

Reaching "Second Generation" Koreans (those of Korean family background who were born in the United States, and whose primary language is English):

Organized by TE Henry Koh, the second MNA Korean English Ministry Pastors' Conference met January 29-31, 2001, at Korean Central Presbyterian Church, Vienna, VA, in the Washington, DC area. The conference theme was Equipping English Ministry (EM) Pastors to Reach the Next Generation. About 80 participated. TE Randy Pope, senior pastor of Perimeter Church in Atlanta, gave most challenging messages as the keynote speaker of the conference.

539

<a id="ga29-p542"></a>
<!-- PAGE ga=29 pdf_page=542 printed_page=540 -->

Through the conference, a number of potential second generation church planters were identified. The prayers of the General Assembly are requested as men train further for this crucial ministry, with its great challenge of reaching people with the Gospel, even as they experience great transition in their own lives and the life of their families and churches. A variety of approaches to church planting is emerging, as first and second generation church planters take up this challenge. As the first and second generations work together, the Gospel will be advanced through the planting of churches that are able to reach and retain second and succeeding generations of Koreans living in North America.

- **C.** Thanksgiving Ministries — Urban and Mercy

The Spirit of the Sovereign Lord is on me, because the Lord has anointed me to preach good news to the poor. He has sent me to bind up the brokenhearted, to proclaim freedom for the captives and release from darkness for the prisoners... Isaiah 61:1

This keynote text for the GA/MNA report is especially applicable to the very important work of MNA Urban and Mercy Ministries. The PCA urban and mercy ministry movement is a growing movement. The Spirit is at work, convincing us of His call to show the mercies of our Lord, even as we preach the Gospel in some of the most challenging communities in North America. And the Lord is blessing, bringing response to the Gospel by the power of His Spirit, along with addressing personal and community needs at a significant level.

A major highlight in the growth of mercy ministries in the PCA was the jointly sponsored MNA/CE&P conference entitled, "The Call of the Gospel: Sharing Christ, Showing Mercy," meeting March 2-3, 2001, in Atlanta. Well attended, this time of worship and training was well received by those wanting to learn from the experience of others how to develop mercy ministries through the local church.

At its March 2001 meeting, the GA/MNA Committee approved the establishing of an Urban and Mercy Ministries endowment fund, to be managed by the PCA Foundation. The purpose of the fund is to build a larger support base for urban and mercy ministries in the PCA, to support both leadership training and direct assistance to people in need. GA/MNA Urban and Mercy Ministries continues its ongoing efforts from the past:

Building the network of communication and resources to encourage urban and mercy ministries, and making them visible to the church and the watching world.

The annual Christian Community Development Association (CCDA) meeting is a gathering point for PCA-affiliated urban and mercy ministries. In 2000, at least 150

540

<a id="ga29-p543"></a>
<!-- PAGE ga=29 pdf_page=543 printed_page=541 -->

from PCA-affiliated ministries attended the CCDA conference in New York. This conference remains the best single place to draw from the expertise, experience and biblical perspective of others engaged in such ministries. In 2001, CCDA will meet in Dallas, November 28 – December 2.

At each General Assembly, GA/MNA sponsors a dinner, at which time the work of one or more urban and mercy ministries is presented. The dinner is open by advance reservation to all who wish to attend.

A directory of PCA-affiliated urban and mercy ministries is available from GA/MNA on request. We invite the churches of the PCA to visit our web site. Since the people and organizations listed in the directory welcome opportunities to encourage and provide consultation in forming new ministries, this directory is a valuable resource for any PCA church who is involved in urban and mercy ministries, or who wishes to begin such ministries in their community. PCA churches and presbyteries are encouraged to avail themselves of the great wealth of experience that already exists in the PCA, as they seek to develop or increase ministry in their own communities.

Leadership development: The Thanksgiving Offering continues to be a resource for encouraging the development of urban and mercy leadership in the PCA. Primarily, the funds are used to sponsor internships for new staff members, seminary students or college students working in urban and mercy ministries. By the end of February 2001, more than $57,000 was received in response to the 2000 Thanksgiving Offering appeal. Beginning with the 11th General Assembly in 1983, Bethany Christian Services has been endorsed by the PCA, upon GA/MNA's annual review and recommendation. We note with gratitude the services of Bethany to thousands of Christian families throughout its 56 years of service, and commend Bethany to the PCA for continued involvement and support. Their report is found as Attachment A.

- **D.** Church Vitality

The mission of GA/MNA Church Vitality is to encourage and equip PCA churches to watch and pray for revival as we work and pray for more vital churches that advance the Gospel. Watching and Praying for Revival The Kingdom Campaign, a strategy based on Acts 1:14-15 to build Kingdom intercessors, enjoyed a healthy start in the year 2000. Local church training events were held in nine cities and presbytery-level training was accomplished in four PCA presbyteries. Plans for 2001 thus far include nine presbytery events and up to ten local church events.

541

<a id="ga29-p544"></a>
<!-- PAGE ga=29 pdf_page=544 printed_page=542 -->

Apprentice training for The Kingdom Campaign has begun, with eight men currently in training. In addition, twelve more men have expressed interest in this ministry, and will be scheduled for training as soon as possible.

Key Covenant Fellowships are designed to help participants in their study of revival, as they continue to watch and pray for it. A text containing discussion guides, called The Spirit of Revival, sold over 10,000 copies in 2000.

In October/November 2000, the third annual Convocation on Revival and Reformation was held at Trinity Presbyterian Church, Jackson, MS. Over 75 pastors and ruling elders studied the Five Pillars of Ministry. Rev. Harry Reeder filled in for James Montgomery Boice who was to have been the plenary speaker. The 2001 Conference, set for November 6-8 is on the theme of "Revival and Reformation in the Book of Acts." J. Eric Alexander will be the plenary speaker.

Working and Praying for More Vital Churches The Embers to a Flame Conference at Briarwood Presbyterian Church in Birmingham, AL, provided training, ideas and encouragement to a record number of pastors and ruling elders, some from as far away as Australia. This conference is the main source of revitalization teaching for churches on a statistical plateau or in decline. An exciting development in this ministry was the translation of the materials into the Korean language. Briarwood held a Korean Embers Conference March 5-8, 2001.

Development work on The Barnabas Institute was put on hold while funding was developed. Once secured, this assessment center for revitalization pastors could be offered in summer 2001.

Materials for Days of Prayer and Fasting continue to be developed and made available to presbyteries, churches and other groups who want to hold this type of event. They are available free upon request.

Pastors-at-Large and Consulting Services are other ministries available to churches and pastors, in order to provide counsel, advice, encouragement and further training in church vitality.

- **E.** Campus Ministries

Reformed University Ministries

Reformed University Ministries of Mission to North America has a goal of building the church now and for the future. This is accomplished by: "Reaching students for Christ and equipping students to serve." That phrase speaks eloquently of our commitment to our covenant children and our obedience to the Great Commission. College years are a time of great opportunity for reaching students with the Gospel. So many testify in later life that their college years were the time when they seriously considered God's truth.

542

<a id="ga29-p545"></a>
<!-- PAGE ga=29 pdf_page=545 printed_page=543 -->

Reformed University Fellowship (RUF) offers the truth of God's Word to students who are searching. By working within the context of the church, the Body of Christ, we follow His leadership as He builds His Kingdom on earth. Students are instructed in Evangelism and Missions, Growth in Grace, Fellowship and Service, and a Biblical World-and-Life View. We are strengthening the church by ministering to covenant children and by evangelizing the lost on campuses across this nation. An ordained PCA minister leads each RUF while actively working to accomplish goals in these four major areas.

Reformed University Fellowship International (RUFI) is reaching out to "all nations," sharing the Gospel of Christ and training Christian internationals to serve Him all over the globe. The hundreds of students involved in RUFI are from at least 40 different countries. Most of these countries are restricted or closed, prohibiting missionaries to serve there. Many of the students return to their own countries to build the Church at home. Our three RUFI missionaries are privileged to introduce internationals to Christ. One of their goals is to help Christian internationals in their struggle to live for Christ in their own cultures.

Campus interns allow a much broader outreach on the campuses. In this learning and ministering position, young men and women, all recent college graduates, work directly with a campus minister, receiving on-the-job-training in evangelism, small group leadership, and one-to-one ministry. A planned program of biblical and theological training accompanies this practical service. After their internship with Reformed University Ministries, interns disperse into the mission field of life, carrying to their future vocations and churches their deepened understanding of God's Word and experience in His service. Truly, campus interns are learning to be "an instrument for noble purposes, made holy, useful to the Master and prepared to do any good work" (II Timothy 2:21 NIV).

Weekly large group, small groups, and one-to-one staff/student meetings provide the structure for campus ministry. Each is essential in ministering to college students. The weekly large group meeting teaches the Word in truth by Bible exposition, examination, and discussion of Scripture. Small groups focus on study, prayer, and fellowship. Oneto-one meetings between students and staff members offer in-depth discipling of Christians, evangelistic encounters and the building of trust-confidence relationships. Each of these three parts supports and strengthens the others. One of the most distinctive things about the ministry of RUF is its emphasis upon the development of a biblical world-and-life view. Only as we see through God's perspective can we understand the truth of any situation. Only as students learn to think biblically will it make a real difference in the Church and the world.

Summer Conference 2000 provided solid Bible exposition for equipping students to better understand and live the Christian life; with teaching, training and equipping in skills related to reaching others for Christ; and fellowship and fun in beautiful

543

<a id="ga29-p546"></a>
<!-- PAGE ga=29 pdf_page=546 printed_page=544 -->

surroundings among Christians from over 48 college and university campuses. It was held May 15-20, 2000 and was extremely well attended. Well over 500 students and 100 staff were able to leave the routine of books and schedules to reflect on life, deal with questions, and be taught from God's Word. The theme of the conference was Sanctification and the Reverend George Robertson from Covenant Presbyterian Church in St. Louis, Missouri expounded the scriptures. Students were eager to receive God's Word. Because of the love of God and the fellowship among other Christians, many new friendships were made. These friendships were used by God to bring students closer to Himself. The 2001 conference, which will address the topic The Sufficiency of Scripture, will be held May 14-19, 2001. Our speakers will be the Reverend Ray Cortese from Seven Rivers Presbyterian Church in Lecanto, Florida, and Dr. Richard Pratt, professor of Old Testament at Reformed Theological Seminary in Orlando, FL.

Conferences provide activities and a relaxing atmosphere as well as a concentrated time for biblical teaching that is new to many students. This teaching is done through elective workshops which the student may choose (two per day), small group study, prayer, and large group teaching each evening. One campus minister rejoiced that, "Many students are understanding the Gospel for the first time and many Christians are being encouraged and strengthened in their walk with God." In addition to Summer Conference, regional Fall, Winter, and Spring conferences are held throughout the year.

In 2000, there were many weeks of training for the field staff. This in-depth training is a distinctive of the ministry and provides philosophical, practical, and reflective instruction to RUF campus ministers, interns, and staff. A Foundations of Campus Ministry Conference was held in Atlanta, Georgia, during August for those interested in learning how Reformed University Ministries does its work, whether church staff, missionary or lay person. This year the conference will be held August 6-9, 2001 at Simpsonwood Conference Center in Atlanta, Georgia.

The year 2000 was a year of record growth as ten new campus ministries were started. The new ministries are: Anderson College, Emory University, Furman University, Millersville University, North Carolina State University, University of Arizona, University of Maryland-College Park, University of Nebraska, University of Virginia, and Yale University. Fill in campus workers were placed at New York University and the University of Southern Mississippi. This growth placed RUF on 56 campuses nationwide, with a hope of reaching 62 total campuses by 2001. Also, we have our largest group of interns yet with 41 in 2000 and 47 expected for 2001. This immense increase in ministry opportunity has greatly challenged our Atlanta staff. Restructuring and changes in personnel have occurred throughout 2000. The beginning of 2001 finds us in possibly our best position in history as far as human resources and the great evidence of God's material blessing to Reformed University Ministries. Reformed University Ministries continues to grow with as many as six new ministries scheduled for 2001.

544

<a id="ga29-p547"></a>
<!-- PAGE ga=29 pdf_page=547 printed_page=545 -->

What is the reason for this growth and excitement? One campus minister told us, "God's Word is alive and active. The Gospel is powerful. That is why RUF is growing RUF seeks to be faithful to God's Word and to biblically minister to students."

In June, 2000, the 28th General Assembly voted overwhelmingly in favor of making Reformed University Ministries a permanent committee of the Presbyterian Church in America. We anticipate the transition to full committee status to be finalized at the 29th General Assembly in June, 2001, with a majority of the presbyteries giving their approval. We are humbled by the confidence placed in us. Along with this trust comes a sense of added responsibility to proclaim the Gospel on college campuses across the country.

Only God could bring together students and ministers from so many different walks of life to accomplish His purposes. Each person that is touched by Reformed University Ministries will, in turn, touch many other people in the course of his or her life. One campus intern noted that, "A true measure of success for RUF... may only be seen in the light of eternity." How true! And how glorious!

Refer to Attachment B for a listing of presbyteries and their affiliated committees, campus staff, location of ministries and the 2002 budget for the entire ministry including affiliated committees for your information.

- **F.** Chaplain Ministries

Just before His ascension, the Lord Jesus Christ commissioned his apostles to go into the entire world and proclaim the Good News. After the resurrection and ascension, the apostles zealously committed themselves to preach the Good News throughout the known world: Jerusalem, Judea, Samaria, and to the ends of the earth. The goal was to ensure that all people, Jew and Gentile, had the opportunity to hear the Gospel and respond to the saving grace of Jesus Christ. Quite often they came under persecution and were banished from living in certain areas of the empire; however, regardless of the cost, they continued on with the mission of permeating the known world with the Gospel of grace. Since the age of the apostles, pastors, evangelists, teachers, missionaries and church members have been commissioned to continue the mission of proclaiming the Gospel to all people throughout the world. Today, among the people who are to be reached with the Good News are those who serve in our government organizations, our military, our hospitals, our prisons and Veteran Affairs.

Although the religious climate has dramatically changed in the post-modern era, still we continue to experience God's blessing upon the ministry of our PCA chaplains and to enjoy the privilege of sending our chaplains into our government institutions. There is still an open door to teach and minister in accordance with the doctrinal teachings of the PCA.

545

<a id="ga29-p548"></a>
<!-- PAGE ga=29 pdf_page=548 printed_page=546 -->

In an article entitled, Missions Today, Bassam Madany writes: "The pulpit may no longer assume that the average western man or woman accepts the uniqueness of the Christian message. We must give biblical reasons for our belief in the uniqueness and finality of the Christian faith." This seems especially true within the society in which our chaplains are called to minister. By the grace of God, more than 70 military active duty chaplains – which represents a significant increase from year 1999 – 50 military reserve or National Guard, 12 Veteran Affairs (full-time and part-time) and approximately 35 prison, hospital, retirement center, Civil Air Patrol and hospice chaplains are communicating the Gospel in their unique settings and giving "biblical reasons for belief in the uniqueness and finality of the Christian faith." In many cases they are communicating the Gospel, pastoring Christians and discipling people who otherwise would not have the opportunity to hear the Word of God, worship in a formal setting or participate in spiritual growth opportunities.

The Primary Mission of GA/MNA Chaplain Ministries remains constant. On behalf of the PCA, the Chaplain Ministries Coordinator is to recruit, send, encourage and oversee chaplains who will be used as God's instruments in faithfully proclaiming the hope of the Gospel to personnel (and their family members) working in our government institutions, hospitals, retirement centers, prisons and various other organizations employing chaplains.

One of the major tasks for the Coordinator is to recruit additional chaplains for all government institutions (military, veteran affairs, prisons). During the year 2000, 12 additional chaplains were recruited and are now serving at their respective locations. Although specific numbers have not been given, the Presbyterian Church in America has been asked to send more.

The Congregational Sponsorship Program greatly assists in meeting one of the primary needs of our chaplains: prayer support. In most cases, military active duty, veteran affairs and prison chaplains do not have the privilege of being immediately involved with a PCA congregation. Consequently, prayer support is limited. Therefore, we continue to enlist sponsoring congregations who will commit to pray for a specific chaplain. Approximately 50% of our chaplains are now sponsored by one or more PCA congregations. The chaplain, in turn, commits to sending a quarterly update on his ministry with specific prayer requests. Congregations that may be interested in supporting this ministry in such a manner may contact the Chaplain Ministries Coordinator.

Keeping in touch with our congregations: The Chaplain Ministries Coordinator and the associate coordinators would enjoy the privilege of informing PCA Congregations of the challenges and joys of Chaplain Ministry. This could be done during a Missions Conference or other special functions sponsored by the Church. Also, the Chaplain Ministries Video is available. There is a fifteen-minute and a five-minute version. Please contact Mission to North America (MNA) if you would like a copy.

546

<a id="ga29-p549"></a>
<!-- PAGE ga=29 pdf_page=549 printed_page=547 -->

The Guardian Prayer Calendar continues to be published quarterly. In addition to specific prayer requests, chaplains provide a short overview of their ministry. Approximately 3000 PCA churches and individuals are on the mailing list. In addition to providing specific chaplain prayer requests, the publication increases the knowledge and awareness of chaplains and their ministry challenges and opportunities.

Financial Support: t: The annual budget for Chaplain Ministries is $150,000. Expenditures include salary, travel, printing, office support and administration. We are very thankful to God that year 2000 for Chaplain Ministries ended in the black. During year 2001 we are praying for an additional 50 congregations who will include Chaplain Ministries in their annual budget.

GA/MNA Chaplain Ministries Volunteers: The Congregational Sponsorship program of Chaplains has become increasingly organized because of the volunteer service of Climie Hewitson, a retired missionary and now member of Good Shepherd Presbyterian Church, Minneapolis, MN. The sponsorship program not only results in prayer for individual chaplains, it also increases the sense of connectionalism between the chaplain and his sponsoring church. Associate Coordinators, CAPT. Stanley J. Beach, USN, RET. and Chaplain Beryl T. Hubbard, COL, RET, USAF provide an immeasurable contribution to this ministry. Their pastoral care of chaplains and their family members, communication with members of our denomination, and assistance with recruiting has reaped significant results and blessing.

The Lord is at work: GA/MNA Chaplain Ministries enjoyed abundant blessing during

2000. The PCA enjoys the privilege of sending a significant number of very gifted, highly motivated and spiritually growing chaplains. Several hundred people have come to a saving knowledge of Jesus Christ as a result of God using them as His instruments. Hundreds of others have been discipled and pastored. The impact chaplains have within their units, hospitals, retirement centers and prisons cannot be measured, but surely it is very significant. In addition to serving on numerous installations in the United States, our chaplains are serving throughout the world, in such places as Kosovo, Bosnia, Germany, Italy, Japan, Korea and Okinawa. Others are serving on ships that are deployed.

One of the great needs in the post-modern era is to faithfully communicate a Christian worldview to the members of the government institutions in which they serve. In almost all cases our chaplains do this well. We thank God for them and for the privilege of working with them and in this ministry.

Refer to Attachment C for the Chaplain Roster.

547

<a id="ga29-p550"></a>
<!-- PAGE ga=29 pdf_page=550 printed_page=548 -->

- **G.** GA/MNA Stewardship

As we trust the Lord to advance the Gospel through Renewing His Church, the Lord calls us to commit our time, talent and treasure to that advancement. GA/MNA seeks to exercise a careful stewardship of all the resources the PCA entrusts to her, and at the same time to encourage the churches and members of the PCA to invest their resources in building the Kingdom. GA/MNA ministries offer the opportunity for the Lord's people to use their resources in this way. From the Apostle Paul, "I thank my God every time I remember you. In all my prayers for all of you, I always pray with joy because of your partnership in the Gospel from the first day until now..." As churches and individuals give of their time, talent and treasure, they enter into a partnership which provides the base for sending the Lord's servants into the harvest field.

Communications: Multiply offers quarterly communication of what the Lord is doing through various ministries of the PCA that advance the Gospel. Weekly content for intercessory prayer with a regional focus is included in each issue. The GA/MNA web site (www.pcanet.org/MNA/) is in the process of being substantially upgraded, and will be built over time into a major resource for all kinds of information and referral sources for ministries related to building the church. The intercessor content for all regions is included on the web site.

Partnership Share/Askings giving: In 2000, church giving to GA/MNA increased 6% over 1999. While GA/MNA expresses gratitude to God for this increase, it must be recognized that such increases provide for a "maintenance" level of ministry at best and do not equip us to advance the Gospel in greater measure. GA/MNA encourages the churches of the PCA to make this giving to all committees and agencies a high priority. The Lord is at work through the PCA in advancing His Kingdom. In order for the PCA to grow stronger over the years, the member churches must be committed to denominational support, just as a particular church can be strong financially only if her members give faithfully. GA/MNA is seeking to build endowment funds, in order to provide greater resources for annual operations and program support.

Church Planting Project Funding: All church planters are supported by gifts designated for their particular projects. GA/MNA invites churches and individuals to consider joining as partners with a church planter, enlisting him as a missionary sent and supported by their church. There are no administrative transfer fees taken from this project support. Every dollar given to a designated ministry or project that is related to GA/MNA is used directly and fully for that ministry or project. Ethnic or multicultural church planters and movement leaders require a special priority for project support. Often the churches they lead in planting

548

<a id="ga29-p551"></a>
<!-- PAGE ga=29 pdf_page=551 printed_page=549 -->

take longer to reach self-support, yet these men often lack the strong networks of family and friends in the PCA who will commit to their support. GA/MNA seeks to establish endowment funds for the support of multicultural church planting, for annual operations support, and for urban and mercy ministries, in order to increase the number of church planters and others who can respond to the call to minister to those in need. The Timothy Fund for Church Planting Apprentices is a special fund to supplement the support of men who have been graduated from seminary, but who need further training before they begin to lead a church plant. Thus far, gifts totaling $462,550 have been contributed to this fund, substantially assisting many apprentices.

Church Vitality and Chaplain Ministries: These two ministries are supported almost entirely by designated gifts, since Partnership Share/Askings giving is insufficient to sustain them. We are grateful to the Lord that both ministries received full support at their current operating level in 2000. However, these ministries fulfill a vital role, and the potential for expansion of ministry is great, as additional resources are provided.

Estate Design and Endowment Services: GA/MNA utilizes and recommends the services of the PCA Foundation in assisting individuals in their stewardship. In addition to the regular PCA Foundation programs, GA/MNA Advise and Consult Funds are also available, managed by the PCA Foundation.

Five Million Fund for Church Buildings: Providing interest-free loans of up to $80,000, this fund continues to be a helpful source for churches as they put together funding packages for their building programs. Though the funds are limited, they often make a difference in the church's ability to qualify for a loan, or they provide additional working cash that is very necessary. This fund is supported by the return payments of the churches to whom loans are made, as well as by donations.

### SUPPLEMENTAL REPORT

### OF THE COMMITTEE ON MISSION TO NORTH AMERICA

### TO THE

### 29TH GENERAL ASSEMBLY OF THE PCA

The Committee on Mission to North America submits the following recommendation as a Supplement to the Report of the Committee on Mission to North America to the 29th General Assembly:

### RECOMMENDATIONS:

13. That the General Assembly elect TE D. Charles (Chuck) Frost to the Presbyterian and Reformed Joint Commission on Chaplains and Military Personnel (PRJC) as a member of the Class of 2005, replacing TE Tom Cheely, elected at the March 2001 GA/MNA Committee meeting. Further, that the MNA Report, Recommendation 13 be amended for this change. (Amended)

18. That Overture 26 from the New York State Presbytery be answered in the affirmative.

19. That Overture 29 From Northern California Presbytery be answered in the negative on the following grounds:

1. Regarding Items 1-4, the overture presents no reasons for requesting this review. There is no self-evident rationale for requiring this review. There are no allegations of impropriety or misuse of funds. Therefore, even the overture itself presents no reasons to proceed with an action that would require a significant expenditure of staff time.

2. Item 4 calls for an adjustment of 1990 - 1997 church planting budgets, based on a standard put in place in 1997. It is not common practice to apply a new standard to previous actions in matters such as this, and there is no rationale offered for doing so in this case.

3. This overture and its requested actions were not supported by Northern California Presbytery, the court to which they were originally presented.

4. Effective January 1, 2000, MNA discontinued the practice of assessing fees on project funds. Since that date, it has been the practice to apply 100% of every designated dollar to the project for which it is designated.

5. Regarding membership in ECFA, the MNA Committee believes that current accountability structures are sufficient to sustain the credibility of the ministry. Its annual audit by an independent accounting firm is reviewed by the MNA Committee and the General Assembly. All aspects of MNA's work are subject to the review of the General Assembly annually. MNA believes that any value gained from ECFA accreditation is more than offset by the time and expense required to maintain such accreditation. 554

### ATTACHMENT A

Bethany Christian Services Report to the 29th General Assembly

We are spending a significant amount of time at Bethany clarifying and planning our ministry vision for the future. In the course of our discussions, we have frequently reflected on the fact that the vision we are planning is not really ours; rather, we are implementing a vision that the Lord has already planned for us.

With that in mind, and however that final vision is articulated, it will inevitably concentrate on fulfilling the Lords' mandate that Christians protect the Sanctity of Human Life and that we minister to orphans, children and families who are hurting.

You may have seen recent reports that the number of children lost to abortion is decreasing. It may in fact be the case that the actual number of abortions occurring in a given year has decreased slightly. However, one life lost is one too many. And, the million and one half that continue to lose their lives every year is stunning. Christians taking responsibility for proclaiming the pro-life message continues to be essential. And, Bethany remains on the front lines of providing compassionate counseling that urges young people to choose life-giving alternatives. Often times a young person's initial contact with Bethany comes through Bethany Lifeline, our toll-free telephone counseling service (staffed entirely by trained volunteers.) This past year, Lifeline received over 11,000 calls. Here are just a few examples of calls received: A woman called immediately prior to leaving for the hospital to deliver her baby. She was terrified because she knew she was not able to be a good mother to her child. One of Bethany's workers immediately went to be with her. Very soon, thereafter, this birth mother chose adoptive planning for her child. A young woman 8 months pregnant and homeless called Bethany Lifeline. One of Bethany's offices found a home for her with one of our foster families. We continue to counsel with her about plans for her and her child. A 22-year-old who is 3 months pregnant called. Her mother told the woman she must get out of the house as soon as her pregnancy started to show. She received Bethany's telephone number from Planned Parenthood. She wonders if we can help her. Sure we can and we will! A 19-year-old called. She is 8 weeks pregnant and just had an abortion several months ago. She is struggling with the guilt she feels over the abortion of her

556

<a id="ga29-p559"></a>
<!-- PAGE ga=29 pdf_page=559 printed_page=557 -->

first child but is still considering aborting her current pregnancy. Our volunteer guided her into counseling at Bethany. She has subsequently chosen life for her child. In counseling sessions, we are also trying to help her see that the Lord will forgive if she asks His forgiveness.

Isn't it interesting to note how Jesus committed Himself to healing while He lived among us? Many of those to whom He ministered and their situations were not pleasant. Likewise, many of the lives Bethany touches are not very easy or pleasant. It takes the forgiving compassion of Christ to care about a young person who has had multiple abortions only to find herself pregnant once again. It takes God's grace and patience to love someone who has put the life of her unborn child at risk by living in a drug culture. It takes incredible love given only by God to care for a 14-year-old who insists she is capable of being a mother all the while trying to help her see and understand the beauty of adoption.

Our counselors daily ask for the Lord's blessing as they deal with these situations. We humbly ask for your continued prayers for those we serve and for those who serve.

But, Bethany's ministry does not stop when the child is born. To who does the gospel of James refer when it challenges us to care for orphans? We could use a narrow definition and look only to children without parents. And, yes, Bethany does find homes for well over 1,400 such children from around the world each year.

But, how about children who are being physically abused or neglected by their parents? How about those who spirits have been broken because of emotional abuse? Or, how about children living with physical or emotional challenges; who live in temporary family foster care or in institutions wondering if anyone will ever care enough about them to adopt them?

Indeed, the challenge is not conquered when the gift of life is assured. Children whose lives are broken and whose spirits and emotions are shattered are our continuing challenge. So... Bethany works together with fellow Christians to minister to these children. In many instances our ultimate goal is finding them permanent Christian families as well.

Bethany has often referred to our relationship with the PCA as a partnership. In reality, though, it is so much more than a partnership. Together we are priests, implementing our Lord's mercy to those who need our care. In some ways it might be easier to use public resources to accomplish that care. Or, it may even be easier to commission Christian ministries like Bethany to answer the call. And, surely much has been gained from developing these resources. In fact, if used very carefully, government funding can frequently be used by Christian ministries to help them reach out in Christ's name. However, removing the opportunity of ministry from each individual Christian moves too far in that direction. By doing so, we rob our Christian community of the privilege,

557

<a id="ga29-p560"></a>
<!-- PAGE ga=29 pdf_page=560 printed_page=558 -->

the joy and of the responsibility of caring for the needs of people. Bethany increasingly sees our mission as that of helping each of you actuate your gifts of caring.

Your congregations and members of your congregations supported Bethany with gifts totaling $1,600,000 this past year. Thank you for that wonderful outpouring of love. We pray and we trust that your support will continue. You also serve on our Boards. We use your facilities. Your open your homes to children. And, most importantly, you pray. Thank you!

As we anticipate the year ahead, we know that many challenges and opportunities will present themselves. Some of the most significant challenges we face include:

1. Sharing the message with many more pregnant young people that adoption is a beautiful alternative:

Unfortunately, less than 1% of those who become pregnant choose the adoption option. And, tragically abortion is the most frequent choice. We need to continue our mission of changing the perception of adoption so that more will choose that plan when it is obviously best for them and their child.

2. Finding Christian homes for children with special life challenges:

Thousands of these children wait for a family. If a member or members of your congregation have love and patience to give such a child, please urge them to call the Bethany office closest to their home.

3. Finding adoptive families for the hundreds of thousands of children living in orphanages around the world:

These are children who cry out for a family to love them. Unfortunately, bureaucratic obstacles often stand in the way of Bethany doing so.

Yes, indeed, we are more than partners. We are fellow Christians. You are Bethany. We are you. We look forward to a year during which we, together, continue our work of extending the love of Christ to children and families in need.

558

<a id="ga29-p561"></a>
<!-- PAGE ga=29 pdf_page=561 printed_page=559 -->

## APPENDIX J

### THE COMMITTEE ON MISSION TO THE WORLD

### TO THE TWENTY-NINTH GENERAL ASSEMBLY

### PRESBYTERIAN CHURCH IN AMERICA

The motto of the Presbyterian Church is "Faithful to the scriptures, true to the Reformed faith, and obedient to the Great Commission." We believe it is this two-fold emphasis that has steered our denomination to the place we find ourselves today. It is, of course, a two-fold and not a three-fold emphasis because the scriptures and the Reformed faith are the same thing.

The truths of scripture and missions have been the two pillars on which the Presbyterian Church in America has been built. Consider these facts which have come from the Stated Clerk of our denomination. The PCA grew at an annual growth rate of 3.16% in

1999. A review of the yearbook of American and Canadian churches over the past ten years indicates that the PCA has frequently been the fastest growing denomination in North America.

In 1973, the year in which the PCA began, we had 260 churches all in the southeastern USA. Today we have 1,415 churches in 49 states and 6 provinces of Canada. We had 196 ministers; today we have 2,873 ministers. We had 40,614 members; in 1999 we had 299,055 members. Total giving to missions in 1973 was $961,835; in 1999 it had grown to $41,500,000.

The actual budget expenses for MTW have grown in the last seven years from $16,684,113 to $32,937,516. According to the Stated Clerk's office, MTW is the largest missionary force of any Presbyterian denomination in history, over 800 missionaries (519 career, 337 two-year term or interns) in 47 countries.

We do not have to argue concerning the purpose of the church. Our Reformed tradition has affirmed for hundreds of years that the sole purpose of the church is to glorify God. The debate always centers around the means by which the church fulfills this purpose. You will find that churches that are growing and vibrant are most often churches that have claimed Acts 1:8 as their own commission from God: "But you will receive power when the Holy Spirit comes on you; and you will be my witnesses in Jerusalem, and in all Judea and Samaria, and to the ends of the earth."

In 1996, we instituted a new strategic plan entitled New Horizon. The missionary force of MTW concluded in the fall of 1999 that we needed to change some of the structures of MTW to better implement New Horizon. This past year we retooled our operations in three ways. First, we made changes in the way we conduct business in seven different areas:

569

<a id="ga29-p572"></a>
<!-- PAGE ga=29 pdf_page=572 printed_page=570 -->

1. Financial customer care - expeditious resolution of missionary financial problems

2. People sourcing – identification of missionary candidates

3. Expense reimbursement – expediting of missionary ministry expenses

4. Candidating – approval of missionary candidates

5. Impact Two-Week – sending of two-week church teams

6. People development – development of missionaries

7. Marketing – communication of MTW's ministry to key stakeholders

Secondly, we are going to review all the policies we have developed over the last 28 years. This will be done by a committee of field personnel who will attempt to eliminate some policies that have outlived their usefulness, and clarify and simplify the rest.

Finally, we have reorganized field operations to include five international directors instead of the present two whose job will be to:

1. Develop and pastor regional team

2. Develop and promote new initiatives

3. Insure performance accountability

4. Coordinate, allocate, and distribute resources

5. Develop strategic partnerships, both with local PCA churches and with national churches

Mission to the World continues to be committed to church planting as the biblical means by which God moves His kingdom work forward. Is New Horizon working? Consider the results we have seen in the Philippines. The goal was to plant 25 churches over a six-year period in Manila and the surrounding provinces. In fact, on February 15, 2000 the MTW church-planting team started their 50th church-planting project. Eight of those have not survived, but 42 of these church plants have national pastors and each of those men has received training from MTW-Philippines in one form or another. We have extensive training activities, consisting of one-on-one mentoring, a large group training, and the church-planting institute conducted by MTW every six months. These national pastors have also been required to take 24 units of special study at the Presbyterian Theological Seminary. The largest of these churches has approximately 300 in attendance, while the smallest ones are still church-planting works in their evangelism and people-finding stages. Of the 42, 28 are the original mother churches, 11 are daughter churches and 3 are granddaughter churches. The strategic plan for the Philippines was clearly based on Acts 1:8. It began in the cities, moved to the provinces, and ultimately to the world. We are delighted to tell you that the churchplanting work in the Philippines has sent its first missionary to Japan to work with our church-planting efforts there. We truly have gone from Jerusalem to the uttermost parts of the world.

We are preparing for a capital campaign for a ministry to street children in the
Philippines. The ministry will revolve around five churches which will be planted with

570

<a id="ga29-p573"></a>
<!-- PAGE ga=29 pdf_page=573 printed_page=571 -->

this specific need as an integral part of their ministry. These five churches will, in turn, grow up around the nine feeding centers that we now have in operation. The goal is for each of these small church-based residential centers to be reaching 150 children at any one time. That is a total of 750 children. We probably will not get the capital campaign off the ground until late summer. Please be in prayer about this.

The street children work, one of our most exciting new ministries at Mission to the
World, is a ministry reaching out to street children around the world. The first model
for this work is moving forward in Lima, Peru. There we have missionaries and
nationals working both with younger children and older teens. We also have works in
Kenya and Romania. We are especially thankful for Opal Hardgrove and the way in
which God has used her to open up these works. She is especially gifted by God
through his Holy Spirit. We are also very thankful to Tom Stewart, a physician who has
given up his practice to oversee this work. We don't know how big this ministry is
going to grow or what places God is going to send us, but we truly believe there will be
significant churches growing up around street children. We also believe that new
dynamic leadership, both for the church of Jesus Christ and for the communities in
which they live are going to come from these ministries. What the gospel does in the
lives of these children who have suffered is going to be a great strength and motivation
for the church at large.

We also started a medical ministry a year and a half ago for physicians, nurses and other medical professionals. In the year 2000 we sent out 239 medical personnel and pastors in this short-term ministry. This is a growing and exciting work. In November we held a conference in Atlanta for medical personnel, and over 420 attended that conference. If you would like a copy of the manual for medical ministries produced by our MTW medical directors, Drs. Ted and Sharon Kuhn, you can order one from our Atlanta office.

We have also reached out to needy people in emergency situations in such places as Honduras, Turkey, and Belize. Even as this report is being written, we are working in India with those whose lives have been devastated by the terrible earthquake. We have a team there now and are preparing to send others, both medical and construction teams. God is using these opportunities to open doors for us to bring the love of Christ to places where it might not otherwise be seen. It also gives the PCA great opportunity to reach out to people in need as our Lord Jesus Christ would do.

In 2000, there were 519 career missionaries, 143 two-year Impact missionaries and 194 intern applicants for a total mission force around the world of 856 missionaries. As well, there were 5,835 short-term summer missionaries. The breakdown of the career missionaries is as follows:

### ASIA/EUROPE HIGHLIGHTS

### ASIA

Australia The Australia University Ministry Team moved to two new levels this year. Their first Australian couple is being trained as national workers, and they took their first group of university students on a missions outreach to Thailand.

Philippines
We began a street children's ministry connected with the local churches. In addition,
the church in the Philippines is sending their first missionary, a two-year, short-term
missionary to Japan.

572

<a id="ga29-p575"></a>
<!-- PAGE ga=29 pdf_page=575 printed_page=573 -->

Taiwan This year Christ's College has the largest number of students ever enrolled. In addition, they began building a new girls' dormitory.

Thailand The team leader and one other member of the team have arrived in country. The team leader is involved in language study. Other team members are in various stages of getting ready to head to the field.

Japan We have had a plan to grow men for ministry and leadership from the university ministry. This year, the first six young men have moved in that direction. One of them is actually going into church planting. Five of the men will return to university work for a period of time, growing and maturing. This is exciting because university ministry is where we expect leadership for the church in Japan to emerge.

Central Asia Two major developments occurred in Central Asia. One, the team has gotten a firm foundation in both language and culture and is beginning to spread out to reach other Central Asian countries and Central Asians in Europe. The second significant development is that a group from the National Presbyterian Church of Mexico visited the work in Central Asia with the idea of eventually sending missionaries from Mexico to work there. It is encouraging to see the people we are working with catch a vision for reaching out to others, not only in their own country, but also around the world.

### EUROPE

Ukraine The government gave us title to a 150-year-old church building in Odessa. Prior to the Bolshevik Revolution, this building belonged to the Reformed church, and the present fledgling denomination was deemed its rightful heir. We undertook a capital campaign to rebuild that church, both because of the legitimacy it offers with the government and the Ukrainian culture. We believe it will provide a home base for ministry throughout Ukraine.

Bulgaria The first Bulgarian trained to be a teaching elder graduated from seminary and began the first church plant with Craig Sheppard, MTW team leader. They have laid a strong foundation for the church with good publication materials, training, and Bible studies.

Germany Will Traub's work with conservative evangelicals from the state church is helping to produce a new "confessing" denomination. The first church is up and running with a pastor. Six more churches have asked to be a part of the group. Only a few actually have pastors, though, so that is a subject of prayer. In addition, they have begun the first Reformed seminary in the German speaking world in many years.

573

<a id="ga29-p576"></a>
<!-- PAGE ga=29 pdf_page=576 printed_page=574 -->

Italy We were well into the Vanguard capital campaign project when we realized that there were other significant events and relationship problems that needed to be dealt with. We have stopped the project at present, but are continuing to be involved in the country.

France The Christian school connected with the church plant in Lyon, after getting off to a rocky start, seems to be settling well into its second year. It has done exceptionally well in providing good public relations for our team among the local people.

Spain Besides the work going in Madrid, we have started a second work in the area around Malaga. Tito Padilla has joined a Spaniard there who has been working at planting Reformed churches.

Portugal The team held its first church-planting seminar inviting missionaries and pastors from around the country. More than 20 missionaries and pastors attended, strengthening and encouraging one another, as well as learning more about church planting. In addition they had the largest summer short-term group they've had in many years. Thirty-five came from the United States as well as eight from South Africa.

Romania
Though we still have not found a team leader for Romania, IMPACT has begun
working there with a Korean missionary. The teams are working with street children
and working alongside Romanians who are being trained for various elder roles.

England Two Welsh congregations have asked to be a part of the Evangelical Presbyterian Church of England and Wales. In addition, our second church planter was accepted. We have also begun working among Central Asians in London.

Scotland We have begun a partnership to help meet the needs of the evangelical conservative churches that are trying to regain a foothold in Scotland. Right now, as in many countries, church membership and attendance is falling off. However, there are several churches that are moving contrary to this stream. We hope to provide assistance in continuing to see other churches move against that flow.

574

<a id="ga29-p577"></a>
<!-- PAGE ga=29 pdf_page=577 printed_page=575 -->

Sweden The team has entered the country now, getting ready for full-time service. They had a strong summer outreach again and are now in the process of selecting the area in which they will work.

### AFRICA/LATIN AMERICA HIGHLIGHTS

### AFRICA/MIDDLE EAST

Senegal will become the provisional team leader of the Senegal church-planting team this year. Frank replaces who is spending more time with the MTW Global Training and Development training efforts. Jeff will be focusing on Francophone training which will keep him involved in Senegal, but also extend his outreach into other areas in Africa and Europe. The work in Senegal continues to grow with three current mission churches and a fourth effort in a relatively unreached part of the city. We are actively seeking others with a call to join the team in order to expand the work.

Cote d'Ivoire Cote d'Ivoire has continued to suffer political upheaval throughout the year. Despite these matters, the work has continued to progress – though we did see two key national leaders and one mission congregation decide that the Lord was leading them to work elsewhere. Our new church-planting effort has kept the number of developing churches at three, one with its own national pastor and another one owning its own building. The newest church plant is looking for a larger place to meet since the living room of the Ivoirian who had the vision to start it can no longer handle the number coming. is involved in a new ministry on the university campus which involves a number of Muslim students and converts from Islam.

Tanzania The team in Dar es Salaam now consists only of but they are actively recruiting people with a variety of skills who can contribute to their effort to plant churches among the Muslims of the city. They are also involved in leadership in Haven of Peace Academy, a school started by several missions, which has a majority of students who are not "missionary kids", including many Tanzanian children and children from Muslim and Hindu families. They have also been able to help local churches move away from a "works" approach to the Christian life.

Sensitive In one country our people have been involved in the production and airing of a video drama on national television which portrayed the problem of guilt and need for a solution. Viewers who respond in writing receive a scripture passage in calligraphy and a regular newsletter. From those who continue to respond, believers will be able to pursue opportunities to present the gospel.

575

<a id="ga29-p578"></a>
<!-- PAGE ga=29 pdf_page=578 printed_page=576 -->

MTW has its first Arab context team that is not in cooperation with a more experienced agency in Muslim ministry. They have been encouraged with a growing group of new believers, men and women, young adults and more mature, who are meeting together regularly for worship and growth. They are part of a committee, including others from Presbyterian perspective, who are planning a presbytery and the training of leadership. Another team, in a more restricted Arab country, had a leader among their small group of potential elders and house church leaders leave the country due to the pressure of his family. Recently the remaining men have started meeting again, and their growth and commitment is encouraging.

MTW has personnel who are training national churches and leadership in facing ministry challenges. We have missionaries ministering to the Fulani of Nigeria, doing Bible translation, medical work, and using other key means to get the gospel where it is least heard. It is encouraging to watch the emerging local churches become lights in these dark places.

Southern Africa Southern Africa is a large and diverse region of the world with many needs and a rich history of church and mission. Until very recently our efforts have focused on the country of South Africa where we are working with national partners in university ministry, theological education and community health. However, new doors of opportunity are opening in Zimbabwe and Zambia as well. We need additional educators, church planting assistants, Muslim ministry workers and administrative support.

AIDS Ministry Mark Mollenkof, MTW missionary in South Africa, reports that he recently had the opportunity to meet with a pastor who is chairman of the governing board of the Missionvale School. The chairman wants Mark to begin an HIV/AIDS awareness program among students and speak to other church leaders in the community. In addition he will train member of the local congregations in counseling and caring for people with AIDS. This is an exciting breakthrough as Mark has tried for the last year to get into the churches in Missionvale to discuss how they can use HIV/AIDS education and counseling as a ministry tool.

### LATIN AMERICA/CARIBBEAN

Chile A leadership-training program has begun in Santiago, Chile, with missionaries and national leaders leading a core group in the context of planting daughter churches. The program provides practical training in church planting, mentoring, and pastoring. There are three full-time candidates, one in Santiago, one in Osorno, and one in Renaca. There is the possibility of having several more in the program soon. The entire training program is designed to prepare men to plant and pastor churches.

576

<a id="ga29-p579"></a>
<!-- PAGE ga=29 pdf_page=579 printed_page=577 -->

Mexico Mission to the World/Mexico is privileged to work alongside the National Presbyterian Church of Mexico (NPC) as it mobilizes its denomination to do church planting both throughout the Republic of Mexico and to other countries. Presently we are working in partnership with over 39 church-planting projects in 19 cities in Mexico. Some leaders of the NPC recently returned from an investigative trip to Turkey as they begin to consider where they will send their first missionaries. To undergird this effort the NPC has formed Movipres, an administrative team to promote Presbyterian church-planting movements. MTW missionaries and PCA churches are working together with Movipres. Over 26 PCA churches have partnered with NPC local churches to support Mexican church planters. In March 2001 the first Church Planters Congress was held in Mexico City to unite and train all the church planters from throughout Mexico. Churchplanting leadership institutes now functioning will begin extension programs in other parts of Mexico. The training of Mexican church-planting mentors is beginning to lend assistance to the church planters. The NPC believes the Lord for 20 new churchplanting projects in 2001.

The year 2001 will be one of leadership transition in Mexico. Jayson and Maureen Kyle, after fourteen years of service in Mexico, will be leaving Mexico City and moving into a ministry to global cities. Maureen is training a missionary to take over her role as the MTW Financial Director for Mexico. Jayson has been serving as MTW's Director for Mexico. We would ask for your prayers as we work through the inevitable changes that come with leadership shifts. Also please pray for the Lord's continued direction and care of the NPC/MTW church-planting partnership and for the church planters and their families.

Haiti Charles Amicy, the national worker in Haiti has planted four churches, each with a trained, Reformed pastor. The fifth church plant should be started in the next few months. Charles is currently training twenty men from three of the four churches to become either elders or future pastors. He is hopeful that a denomination will be formed by the end of 2001. Medical teams from the United States have been doing outreaches about four times a year. A site and design for a medical clinic have been chosen, and a Haitian doctor has enthusiastically agreed to be a part of this when it is established.

Hinterland The Cusco Presbyterian Church of San Jeronimo met March 4, 2001 to organize as an official church of the Reformed Presbyterian Church of Peru Denomination. They have a Peruvian session of one teaching elder and two ruling elders as well as a communicant membership of approximately 40. They have 10 people presently in training as church leaders as well as two pastoral candidates in training. Perhaps the most interesting thing about this group is their involvement in about 10 church-planting efforts in essentially unreached towns and villages.

577

<a id="ga29-p580"></a>
<!-- PAGE ga=29 pdf_page=580 printed_page=578 -->

Belize There are currently two career units and three two-year units ministering in Belize. There are also two units currently raising support to go to Belize. There were 16 interns in Belize who worked in a variety of ministries: medical, education, children's ministry, youth ministry, and ministry support. In addition there were 630 one-and two-week people who worked on 12 different construction sites, conducted 16 Vacation Bible Schools, six youth outreaches, and three adult training seminars. A two-week team also held an Evangelism Explosion Clinic at one of the Belizean churches.

MTW has also been participating with the Belize Presbytery in providing theological education materials from Covenant Theological Seminary. The Belize City Church has completed two courses: Life and Teaching of Jesus and Man, Christ and Redemption. The church in San Narciso has complete one course, Biblical Theology.

Honduras In the spring of 2000, Honduras was approved as a new field for MTW. There are three units preparing to go to Honduras for at least two years, and they began cross-cultural training in March of 2001. The focus of ministry has been to the island of Guanaja. We have been doing relief work, evangelism and Bible studies. There were seven interns and 101 one- and two-week teams that went to Honduras in 2000.

### RECOMMENDATIONS

The Committee on Mission to the World makes the following recommendations to the Twenty-Ninth General Assembly of the Presbyterian Church in America:

1. That the month of October 2001, be set aside as a month of prayer for the "10/40 Window" and world evangelization, and that God would send many more laborers into His harvest field.

2. That the General Assembly urge the churches to set aside a portion of their giving for the suffering peoples of the world; to that end be it recommended that a special offering for relief and mercy (Compassion Ministry) be taken during 2002 to be distributed by MTW.

3. That the General Assembly set aside Sunday, November 11, 2001, as a day of prayer and fasting for the persecuted church worldwide.

4. With gratitude to God for the life, ministry, and service of Paul D. Kooistra, the Committee on Mission to the World enthusiastically recommends that Dr. Kooistra be re-elected as Coordinator of Mission to the World.

5. That the proposed budget of MTW, as presented through the Administrative Committee, be approved.

6. That the minutes of the meeting of March 8-10, 2000, be accepted.

7. That the minutes of the meeting of November 1-3, 2000, be accepted.

Respectfully submitted, /s/ L. B. Austin III, Chairman Committee on Mission to the World 578
