## APPENDIX K

### MINUTES OF THE

### NOMINATING COMMITTEE OF THE

### TWENTY-NINTH GENERAL ASSEMBLY

### OF THE PRESBYTERIAN CHURCH IN AMERICA

The General Assembly's Nominating Committee convened in Atlanta, Georgia, at the Holiday Inn Select Hotel on Saturday, March 24, 2001. Chairman RE David Moon called the meeting to order at 9 AM and TE Dan Barr opened with prayer.

The roll call was made by the Secretary. Thirty-six were present, including TE L. Roy Taylor, PCA Stated Clerk, as a visitor.

Ascension RE William Mitchell (2003) Calvary TE Richard Thomas (2003) Central Carolina RE Harold Jones (2002) Central Georgia TE John C. Jagoditsch (2002) Eastern Carolina TE Ben Inman (2002) Evangel TE Frank Barker (2001) Gulf Coast TE Bruce Sinclair (2003) Heritage TE Jim Brown (2003) James River RE Clyde Vick (2003) Korean Southeastern TE Young Pal Cho (2001 Louisiana TE Paul Lipe (2001) Metropolitan NY RE Clayton Prugh (2002) New Jersey RE Dan Barr (2001) New River RE Harry Musser (2001) North Florida TE William Lamkin (2001) North Georgia RE John Rollo (2001) North Texas RE M. C. Culbertson (2001) Pacific TE J. Phillip Clark (2002) Pacific Northwest RE Don Robertson (2002) Palmetto TE P. Cameron Kirker (2003) Philadelphia TE Erwin Morrison (2001) Pittsburgh TE Harold Kelley (2001) Potomac TE Tom Osterhaus (2001) Rocky Mountain TE Steve Reese (2003) South Texas RE Claude Roberts (2002) Southeast Alabama TE Stephen Estock (2002) Southeast Louisiana RE Edwin M. Hackenberg (2001) Southern Florida TE R. Lynn Downing (2001) Southern New England TE Rick Downs (2002) Southwest RE David Moon (2001) Southwest Florida RE Henry Whitmore (2003) Susquehanna Valley RE W. Lee Troup (2003) Warrior RE James Albritton (2003) 584

<a id="ga29-p587"></a>
<!-- PAGE ga=29 pdf_page=587 printed_page=585 -->

Western Carolina RE Ed Robeson (2002) Westminster RE Joe Reynolds (2002)

Stated Clerk, Roy Taylor, informed the Committee that TE Frederic Mau had resigned from the Administration Committee, Class of '04, and that TE Michael Milton had replaced him.

Matters related to the nomination process for the PCA Foundation with respect to proposed by-law changes to be considered at this year's General Assembly were referred to a Nominating Committee sub-committee.

Chairman Moon read and commented on Acts 1:21-26. A season of prayer followed which was begun by Roy Taylor and concluded by Mr. Moon.

Subcommittee assignments were made and the main meeting divided into the subcommittees for deliberation. The sub-committees concluded their work and were dismissed for lunch around noon.

The Nominating Committee, as a whole, reconvened from lunch at 1 PM and was led in prayer by Chairman Moon. Reports of the subcommittees were presented in order to finalize the nominees to be presented to General Assembly.

The Committee elected TE Jack Jagoditsch, Central Georgia Presbytery, Chairman and RE William Mitchell, Ascension, Secretary of the 2002 GA Nominating Committee.

The next meeting of the Nominating Committee will be at General Assembly on Wednesday, time and place to be announced.

Next year's Spring meeting will be Saturday, March 23, 2002. The meeting was closed in prayer by Chairman Moon at 3:15 p.m.

Resp sub

RE David Moon, Chrm TE Jack Jagoditsch, Clerk

The General Assembly's Nominating Committee convened in Dallas, Texas, at the Adam's Mark Hotel on June 21, 2001 at 7:45 AM. Chairman RE David Moon called the meeting to order and led in prayer. The roll was taken by the Secretary and the Committee members with their Presbytery as follows:

Ascension RE William Mitchell Central Georgia TE John C. Jagoditsch Palmetto TE Cameron Kirker Philadelphia TE Erwin Morrison Potomac TE Tom Osterhaus Southern New England TE Rick Downs Southwest RE David Moon Southwest Florida RE Henry Whitmore Susquehanna Valley RE Lee Troup Westminster RE Joe Reynolds

The purpose of the meeting was to deal with an irregularlity not identified previously. The irregularity involved one person receiving duplicate nominations for the same position. It was moved, seconded and passed by the Committee to waive the irregularity. The meeting was closed with prayer by TE Rick Downs at 8:00 AM.

Respectfully submitted

RE David Moon, Chairman TE Jack Jagoditsch, Secretary (Clerk)

## APPENDIX L

### PRESBYTERIAN CHURCH IN AMERICA

### FOUNDATION, INC.

### REPORT TO THE 29TH GENERAL ASSEMBLY

The PCA Foundation is pleased to report that it has just completed 2000 on a self-supported basis. This has been a goal that we have been striving toward for three years. The Lord continues to bless the work of the Foundation.

There were several other noteworthy events in 2000. The Foundation reached new record levels for gifts, distributions to ministry, and total assets. Also, we took a big step forward by hiring a Vice President - Development to help continue with our growth and effectiveness.

Total assets as of December 31, 2000 reached $25.0 million - a new record. This is an increase of $2.6 million, or 12% from the 1999 year-end amount of $22.4 million. It is significant to note that, while growth in total assets is important, it does not tell the whole story about what the Foundation does and will accomplish in its ministry. So much of what we do results in gifts coming into the Foundation and going right back out as distributions to ministries within a relatively short period of time- often within the same year. Therefore, the Foundation realizes significant amounts as both gifts and distributions in a given year, yet may not experience a substantial change in total assets.

The most significant contribution to the increase in total assets was the continued growth of the Foundation's Advise and Consult Fund, a donor advised fund, which increased to $7.4 million as of 12/31/00 from $5.5 million at the end of 1999, an increase of $1.9 million or 35%. This $1.9 million net increase resulted from contributions to the Advise and Consult Fund of $7.0 million, less distributions to Christian ministries totaling approximately $5.1 million.

Total gifts to the Foundation during 2000 also reached a new milestone - $9.2 million. This compares to $5.8 million in 1999, an increase of $3.4 million or 59%. As mentioned above, $7.0 million of this amount consisted of contributions to the Advise & Consult Fund, and the remainder represents contributions by individuals to Endowment Funds, Charitable Remainder Trusts, Designated Funds and other miscellaneous contributions.

Distributions, or grants to ministry, also reached an all time high during 2000 -- $6.1 million. This compares to $3.5 million in 1999, an increase of $2.6 million or 74%. The

615

<a id="ga29-p618"></a>
<!-- PAGE ga=29 pdf_page=618 printed_page=616 -->

increase in distributions was primarily to PCA churches: $3.8 million in 2000 compared to $1.5 million in 1999 – an increase of $2.3 million or 153%.

The Foundation's total 2000 fund raising, management and general expenses as a percentage of all expenses and grants was only 8%, well below the industry average of 16%, as compiled by Capin Crouse, LLP, the Foundation's accountants. The 2000 distributions (grants) to ministry by the Foundation were as follows:

Mission to the World $188,000 Mission to North America 171,000 Christian Education and Publications 15,000 Administrative Committee 15,000 IAR-Ministerial Relief 13,000 Reformed University Ministries 34,000 Covenant College 64,000 Covenant Seminary 332,000 PCA Foundation 143,000 Ridge Haven 13,000 Total Committees & Agencies 988,000

PCA Churches 3,847,000 Other Christian Ministries 1,301,000 Total $6,136,000

It has been exciting to see how the Lord used the Foundation during 2000 in Kingdom ministry.

During 2000, we began aggressively marketing Designated Funds for churches, presbyteries, and other ministries. This service has been well received, and we believe that it will be used by more churches, presbyteries, and ministries as we continue to market this service to them. By setting up a Designated Fund with the Foundation, a church, presbytery or ministry specifies the intended use of the Fund, and controls the distributions from it. The Foundation invests and administrates the Fund, and can process various types of gifts, including appreciated assets.

The Foundation plans to continue vigorously promoting and providing its services to individuals and families, churches, presbyteries and ministries, as well as provide services to PCA Committees and Agencies whenever possible.

Because the focus of the Foundation is not on raising funds for its own operations, it has a unique opportunity and niche. Our ministry is providing services and financial vehicles to help Christians to carry out their stewardship responsibilities, as well as offering services and financial vehicles to churches, presbyteries and other ministries. The Foundation is

616

<a id="ga29-p619"></a>
<!-- PAGE ga=29 pdf_page=619 printed_page=617 -->

"Kingdom focused" and "donor driven," which means that we work on the donor's agenda, not our own. We provide charitable services to individuals without pressuring them to give to the PCA Foundation, or any other ministry. The result is more money for ministry.

Now that the Foundation has successfully achieved self-supporting status and no longer receives General Assembly mandated support from Committees and Agencies, our Board is recommending that the Board itself be re-constituted so that all ten of its members are elected at large by the General Assembly, rather than have four of its members appointed from the Boards and Committees of other PCA Committees and Agencies. The Foundation Board recognizes the necessity of this in order to enable the Foundation to better represent and serve the Church at large. The Foundation will continue to invite representatives from all Committees and Agencies to attend its Board meetings.

The Foundation will also continue to strive to effectively meet the needs of its present and future donors, as well as the PCA: its churches, presbyteries, Committees, and Agencies.

By God's grace, the result of our work will be a continued increase in the gifts to the Foundation, distributions to ministry from the Foundation, and growth of the Foundation's total assets.

We ask that you continue to pray for the Board and staff of the Foundation as they seek to continue leading the Foundation successfully into the future.

### RIDGE HAVEN REPORT TO THE TWENTY-NINETH

### GENERAL ASSEMBLY

### PRESBYTERIAN CHURCH IN AMERICA

Ridge Haven exists as a camp, conference, retreat center, and residential community to proclaim the gospel to the lost, nurture God's people in the truth of God's word, and provide a place of rest, refuge, and renewal so that God is glorified and God's people are challenged and equipped for service and ministry in His kingdom. – The Ridge Haven Purpose Statement

Ridge Haven More than you can imagine and better than you remember!

The following words of testimony and many others are multiplied each year more than 8000 times. Surely the Lord has blessed the PCA with the extraordinary resource of Ridge Haven!

Kennedy Smartt was awesome!! Dean was great! I loved the Kirk Ward band! - YoWAW student.

God has spoken clearly to me in ways that perhaps a seminar was never intended to do; the power of His word is clearly evident! But what is really tremendous is when God uses these dynamic young people to minister and convict us old people! It is such an encouragement to see such great kids in one place. YoWAW has found a great balance; and the young people respond to it with hearts that don't soon forget what God has revealed to him. Thank you, thank you for your dedication, your servants' hearts, your labors – we pray for you and thank God for you!! – YoWAW adult leader.

This time at Ridge Haven has been a time of spiritual refreshment for me. The interaction with God's people from many places has been rich and encouraging... It has been a blessing! – Covenant Family Conference.

Keenagers is the highlight of our year. We look forward to it each year... It is a week of spiritual growth and rest as we sit under the ministry of our Lord through all of you at Ridge Haven. It is truly a haven for the weary soul and a time of refreshing and building us up to continue the ministries we are called to in our local churches. – Keenager Conference.

I have also made some of my best friends and experienced some of my best times while at Ridge Haven... – Camper.

This place has been rest and solace to our weary souls and bodies. – An individual guest.
